name: Seychellois fish curry
subtitle: Fish curry belongs to the coconut curries counted among Seychellois specialities, in a cuisine shaped by Indian, Chinese, African, French and English influences and marked by careful blending of spice

facts.label: Type of dish
facts.value: Coconut curries are among the Seychellois specialities

facts.label: Fish in the cuisine
facts.value: Fresh fish is a main element of most Seychellois dishes and may be grilled, roasted, fried, curried or made into salads

facts.label: Influences
facts.value: Seychellois cuisine draws on Indian, Chinese, African, French and English origins

facts.label: Spices and coconut
facts.value: Careful blending of spices is the cuisine's main feature; coconut milk is used very often

facts.label: Choice of fish
facts.value: Red snapper or grouper, because the flesh does not fall apart easily when cooked

facts.label: Aromatics
facts.value: Curry leaves and a cinnamon leaf

facts.label: Main ingredients
facts.value: Firm white fish such as snapper, cooked in coconut milk

parts.text: Fish curry belongs to the coconut curries counted among Seychellois specialities, in a cuisine shaped by Indian, Chinese, African, French and English influences and marked by careful blending of spices. Firm fish such as red snapper or grouper is cooked with curry powder, turmeric, curry leaves and coconut milk.
Published Seychellois recipes serve it with rice: coconut rice in one, Creole rice in another.

blocks.title: Seychelles fish curry (Rakesh Pultee, Raffles Seychelles)
blocks.sub: One version of the dish, as given by Sunday Times (TimesLIVE), South Africa; the steps are summarised in our own words. Recipes differ from cook to cook.
blocks.note: Recipe by a sous chef at Raffles Seychelles, published by the South African Sunday Times; the source also gives a coconut rice recipe.

ingredients.name: fresh firm white fish (e.g. snapper), cubed

steps.text: Warm the oil in a large pan and fry the ginger-garlic paste, onion, curry leaves and cinnamon.
Stir in the cumin, curry powder and turmeric and let them cook briefly.
Add the fish and toss it in the pan until coated with the spice mixture.
Season, add the chillies, cloves and coconut milk and cook.
Check the seasoning and cook a little longer, then serve with coconut rice.
